$comment: ADR-467: rivers that flood — a heavy rain or storm swells sea-level water onto low shore ground (at most maxDistance tiles out), the flood water is natural water (so it freezes in winter, ADR-450), and it recedes GRADUALLY over in-game time (Tracey: never a single-step clear). Spring melt raises the lake level by 1 tile (seasonal band); summer drains it, again gradually. Flood water never touches an elevated lake or a spillway (waterfall rule, ADR-383/386): the flood only spreads from sea-level water (surface 0) and never floods a tile adjacent to water whose surface is not 0. Times are in-game seconds (20 ticks/s); a game day is 3600 s (24 game-hours, so 1 game-hour is 150 s). drainAfterSeconds 900 = the flood stays 6 game-hours after the tile floods, then the outermost tiles drain first, one distance step every 2 game-hours (drainStepSeconds 300), so a 3-tile flood recedes edge-inward over 4 game-hours.
